### Supplemental Materials

#### P-Hacking

1.  [**P-Hacking Demonstration**](https://stats.andrewheiss.com/hack-your-way/)**.** A recreation of a great interactive demonstration of how you can say anything with the "right" linear model.
2.  [**Tsang, B. (2025). P hacking—five ways it could happen to you. *Nature*, *10***](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/qvzu81r7xkdifrybc1753/PhackingFivewaysitcouldhappentoyou.pdf?rlkey=ixxwyu3tuefn1dbgwhjyxtx7g&dl=0)**.** Do you think fear mongering is good if it's in the interest of valid science?
3.  [**Data Colada**](https://datacolada.org)**.** Thoughts on quality control in the social science. These authors have shed light on (and taken down) some big names in the field.

#### **Multiple Comparisons Problem.** 

The more analyses you run, the more likely you'll reject the null due to chance.

1.  [a comic. haha](https://www.explainxkcd.com/wiki/index.php/882:_Significant).
2.  [a blog post](https://methods.egap.org/guides/analysis-procedures/multiple-comparisons_en.html) outlining the different problems and some possible solutions.
3.  [a more serious article](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5506159/) on the problem of multiple comparisons, and methods to make corrections.

#### Construct Validity

1.  [**A thorough article**](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7954782/) on different types of construct validity in psychology.
